S4–S7 walkthrough

S4–S7 walkthrough: blocks, placement, routing, extraction and post-layout SPICE

Generated by python3 scripts/make_s4s7_walkthrough.py from the run’s own output files (repo at 7839123d4 2026-11-04). Every number below is read from outputs/. Typed by hand: the meaning of each gate, the explanation of each known finding, and the How to read it notes. The companion page docs/s0_s3_walkthrough.html covers S0–S3 (its reading guide applies here too); the plans are docs/plan_v4_S4_S7.md and, for ttsky25a_fd, docs/plan_v5_ttsky25a.md; the record is docs/flow_record.md sections 7.15–7.23.

The four stages:

  • S4: Blocks: groups S3’s ringless cells into blocks (matching groups first; one device type and one body per block), draws the variants (A, AB mirror image, ABBA common centroid, ABAB interdigitated, or a row), closes each with one tap ring (tap strips where a row is too wide), draws a bound MIM capacitor as its own block, and signs every variant off with DRC and LVS. A design’s inputs/<d>/layout.yaml can ask for more (Phase 8): m copies drawn as units in common-centroid or interdigitated rows only, a dummy at each end of every matched row, matched resistor strings interleaved in one block, and MIM arrays.
  • S5: Placement and routing: enumerates every row partition (PMOS above NMOS, in the designer’s row order), variant and flip, scores each twice (budget-aware: area plus S2’s wire budgets; area-only: the AICL-like baseline), routes both winners with one metal-4 spine per net, and signs them off (DRC, LVS, S2’s route rules). A design with its own hierarchy (hierarchy: upstream) is placed by macros instead: each sub-circuit placed by seeded annealing in three shapes, every arrangement of the shapes tried inside the hard outline, then routed on a metal3/metal4 grid.
  • S6: Extraction: Magic extracts each routed layout capacitance-only and R+C (unless the design switches R+C off), LVS-checks the extraction, and compares every budgeted parasitic of S2 with what was extracted.
  • S7: Post-layout SPICE: the schematic, the drawn devices, the C-only and the R+C netlists in S0’s own benches; each spec’s loss against eta × margin (on the C-only netlist where there is no R+C).

Status per design:

Design S4 S5 S6 S7
example_ota_5t PASS PASS PASS PASS
loadbench_miller PASS FAIL FAIL FAIL
ttsky25a_fd PASS FAIL FAIL FAIL

Two more ideas this page uses (the rest are in the S0–S3 page’s reading guide):

  • Budget-aware and area-only. S5 scores every placement twice: by area plus S2’s wire budgets (the flow’s own rule) and by area alone (the baseline of the AICL paper). Both winners are routed by the same router, so the two layouts differ only in the placement; that comparison is hypothesis H5.
  • H4. If every parasitic stays within its S2 budget (G6.2), the layout should keep every spec within eta × margin (G7.1, G7.2).

How to read it. Each column is the winner of one cost. A net’s wire-budget use is its length over S2’s maximum length for it (1.0 = the limit): first the placer’s half-perimeter estimate, then the routed wires. The budget-aware cost adds 10 × any excess and the uses themselves to the area; the area-only cost is the area alone.

What it shows here: at 1 × the area-only area, the budget-aware placement uses less of the budget on OUTP, net1 and net3; after routing, every net is within its length budget; G5.7: budget-aware: 0 of 2 matched blocks common-centroid (the others: pmos_current_mirror_load AB and nmos_differential_pair AB); area-only: 0 of 2 matched blocks common-centroid (the others: pmos_current_mirror_load AB and nmos_differential_pair AB).

How to read it. The routed layouts, budget-aware first. PMOS blocks are above NMOS; the vertical purple lines are the metal-4 spines, one per net, joined to the blocks’ metal-3 tracks by vias.

Known findings (failed gates and why; none is a crash):

  • S5 G5.4 (the routes meet S2’s route rules: length, parallel runs, series R against what S3 left, symmetry): outFirstStage joins the input pair, the mirror, N3’s gate and the Miller capacitor, and S2 allows it 16.3 µm of metal3; no row placement of these blocks gets it under 1.65 × that. The input pair’s series-R budget was already used by S3’s cells (the known G3.5 relaxation), so no wire fits in it.
  • S6 G6.2 (every budgeted net capacitance, coupling and terminal R of the budget-aware layout within S2’s budget): the largest excesses sit at the Miller capacitor: its own fringe and bottom-plate capacitance land on out and outFirstStage, and S2’s budgets were set without them (G6.5 shows the part that is very likely counted twice). The input pair’s terminal R is over because S3’s cells already used it.
  • S7 G7.2 (each spec loses at most eta × margin from schematic to post-layout): GBW loses more than eta × its 2.34 MHz margin. GBW is about gm1 / Cc, and the out~outFirstStage coupling sits beside the 0.5 pF Miller capacitor; most of it is the capacitor’s own plate-to-plate coupling as Magic extracts it, very likely counted twice (G6.5). With that coupling cancelled (G7.5) every spec stays within eta × margin; every spec is met either way (G7.1).

How to read it. The same benches as S0, with the circuit replaced by each view of the layout: drawn devices only, then every capacitance, then capacitance and wire resistance (the post-layout result). The loss is how much of the margin the layout takes; 1.0 is all that eta allows (bold: more).

What it shows here: every spec is met post-layout; the largest loss is gbw_mhz at 1.08 of eta × margin (over); H4: G6.2 failed and G7.1/G7.2 did not both pass; with the capacitor’s own plate coupling cancelled, gain_db uses 0.0336, gbw_mhz uses 0.575, pm_deg uses 0.209.

ttsky25a_fd

Run: ./flow run ttsky25a_fd --from S4. Status, run time and the steps of each stage:

Stage Status Started Run time Steps
S4 PASS 2026-11-04T13:16:36 4.2 min run

Known findings (failed gates and why; none is a crash):

  • S5 G5.4 (the routes meet S2’s route rules: length, parallel runs, series R against what S3 left, symmetry): S2’s length budgets assume a far more compact layout than blocks with tap rings, dummies and 3 µm gaps in a 250 × 200 µm outline: every net that crosses sub-circuits is over (net6 and Vom the most). The rest of the gate (series R through S3’s cells, the symmetric-route rules the grid router does not draw) fails as on LOADBench.
  • S6 G6.2 (every budgeted net capacitance, coupling and terminal R of the budget-aware layout within S2’s budget): follows from G5.4: the long cross-sub-circuit nets and their couplings, and the Miller capacitors’ own plate coupling (G6.5), are over S2’s capacitance budgets.
  • S7 G7.2 (each spec loses at most eta × margin from schematic to post-layout): GBW loses 0.13 MHz, 63 % of its 0.205 MHz margin, above eta = 0.5; every spec is still met (G7.1). About two thirds of it is the Miller capacitors’ plate coupling that Magic very likely counts twice: with it cancelled (G7.5) GBW uses 0.45 of the allowance. Measured C-only (R+C is off for this design, flow record row 87), like the hand-drawn tile.

S4

Blocks: groups S3’s ringless cells into blocks (matching groups first; one device type and one body per block), draws the variants (A, AB mirror image, ABBA common centroid, ABAB interdigitated, or a row), closes each with one tap ring (tap strips where a row is too wide), draws a bound MIM capacitor as its own block, and signs every variant off with DRC and LVS. A design’s inputs/<d>/layout.yaml can ask for more (Phase 8): m copies drawn as units in common-centroid or interdigitated rows only, a dummy at each end of every matched row, matched resistor strings interleaved in one block, and MIM arrays.

Outputs: outputs/S4/ttsky25a_fd/ (report: s4_report.json).

How to read it. One row per drawn variant of each block. The tap distance is how far the farthest diffusion stands from its ring or a tap strip; S2’s latch-up rule allows 15 µm. A mirror image means every unit faces a flipped copy across the centre (AB, ABBA); ABAB is interdigitated, not a mirror image.

What it shows here: 33 blocks, 53 variants, all signed off; no block needed a tap strip; XC1 is drawn as sky130_fd_pr__cap_mim_m3_1 (10 × 10 µm, 5 units, PDK device in the netlist), top plate on Vop1, bottom plate on Vom; XC2 is drawn as sky130_fd_pr__cap_mim_m3_1 (10 × 10 µm, 5 units, PDK device in the netlist), top plate on Vom1, bottom plate on Vop; res_packs holds 40 resistors as matched strings, interleaved in one block.

How to read it. The first variant of each block as drawn: the units in a row, metal-2 stubs to one metal-3 track per net above and below, and the ring around everything (n-well for PMOS).

S5

Placement and routing: enumerates every row partition (PMOS above NMOS, in the designer’s row order), variant and flip, scores each twice (budget-aware: area plus S2’s wire budgets; area-only: the AICL-like baseline), routes both winners with one metal-4 spine per net, and signs them off (DRC, LVS, S2’s route rules). A design with its own hierarchy (hierarchy: upstream) is placed by macros instead: each sub-circuit placed by seeded annealing in three shapes, every arrangement of the shapes tried inside the hard outline, then routed on a metal3/metal4 grid.

Outputs: outputs/S5/ttsky25a_fd/ (report: s5_report.json).

How to read it. Each column is the winner of one cost. A net’s wire-budget use is its length over S2’s maximum length for it (1.0 = the limit): first the placer’s half-perimeter estimate, then the routed wires. The budget-aware cost adds 10 × any excess and the uses themselves to the area; the area-only cost is the area alone.

What it shows here: at 1.24 × the area-only area, the budget-aware placement uses less of the budget on NBias, PBias, Vom1, Vop, Vop1, net1, net2, net3, net4, net5, net6, x1_Vtest2, x1_net1, x1_net2, x1_net4, x1_net6, x1_net7, x1_net8, x2_Vbiasp, x2_Vcm and x2_net1; after routing, 16 nets still exceed their budgets: Vom, Vom1, Vop, Vop1, net5, net6, net7, x1_Vbias, x1_Vout, x1_Vtest2, x1_net1, x1_net2, x1_net5, x1_net6, x1_net7 and x1_net8; G5.7: budget-aware: 13 of 20 matched blocks common-centroid (the others: mirror_XX1_M1_XX1_M2_XX1_M7_XX1_M9 interdigitated, pmos_current_mirror ABAB, pmos_current_mirror_load ABAB, nmos_matched_current_source_pair ABAB, pmos_matched_current_source_pair ABAB, pmos_matched_current_source_pair_2 ABAB and pmos_matched_cascode_pair ABAB); area-only: 6 of 20 matched blocks common-centroid (the others: nmos_differential_pair ABAB, nmos_differential_pair_2 ABAB, nmos_differential_pair_3 ABAB, nmos_current_mirror interdigitated, mirror_XX1_M22_XX1_M15 ABAB, nmos_current_mirror_3 ABAB, pmos_current_mirror ABAB, pmos_current_mirror_load ABAB, nmos_matched_cascode_pair_2 ABAB, nmos_matched_current_source_pair ABAB, pmos_matched_current_source_pair_2 ABAB, pmos_matched_current_source_pair_3 ABAB, pmos_matched_cascode_pair ABAB and pmos_matched_current_source_pair_4 ABAB).

How to read it. The routed layouts, budget-aware first. Each sub-circuit is a group of rows (PMOS above NMOS inside it); the top-level nets run on a 0.8 µm grid, metal-3 horizontal and metal-4 vertical, joined to the blocks’ metal-3 tracks by metal-4 stubs and vias.

How to read it. Every parasitic S2 budgeted, as extracted from the routed layout: net capacitance to an AC ground, coupling between two signal nets (fF), and terminal resistance (Ω, S3’s cell plus S5’s wires and vias). Use is extracted / budget; bold marks an element over its budget. Only the 40 most used of 2676 elements are listed; all are in outputs/S6/ttsky25a_fd/parasitics_vs_budgets.json.

What it shows here: 195 of 2676 elements are over budget, the worst x1_net4~x1_net5 at 54.1 ×; Magic’s C-only netlist holds 48 % less capacitance than its .ext (G6.4); the XC1 block alone carries 48.5 fF between its plates (very likely counted twice, G6.5) and 26.9 fF from its bottom plate to the substrate; the XC2 block alone carries 48.5 fF between its plates (very likely counted twice, G6.5) and 26.9 fF from its bottom plate to the substrate.

How to read it. The same benches as S0, with the circuit replaced by each view of the layout: drawn devices only, then every capacitance, then capacitance and wire resistance (the post-layout result). The loss is how much of the margin the layout takes; 1.0 is all that eta allows (bold: more). This design has no R+C extraction, so the C-only netlist is the post-layout result and the loss is measured on it.

What it shows here: every spec is met post-layout; the largest loss is gbw_mhz at 1.27 of eta × margin (over); H4: G6.2 failed and G7.1/G7.2 did not both pass; with the capacitors’ own plate coupling cancelled, gain_db uses 0.278, gbw_mhz uses 0.455, pm_deg uses 0.593.
